questions.question_english: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): No principal employer of an unregistered establishment can legally employ contract labour. Reason (R): Section 9 of the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970 expressly prohibits the employment of contract labour in an establishment that is required to be registered but has failed to do so.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: Assertion A correctly states that an unregistered establishment cannot legally engage contract labour. questions.topic: Contract Labour Abolition and Regulation Act 1970
key_facts: Section 9 prohibits employment of contract labour in unregistered establishments.
Printed answer key: (A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.question_english: In relation to a factory, who among the following is designated as the Principal Employer under the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970?

The Owner or Occupier of the factory
The Chief Inspector of Factories appointed by Government

questions.explanation_english: Section 2(1)(g)(ii) defines the Principal Employer in respect of a factory as the owner or occupier of the factory, including the managing agent of such owner or occupier. This statutory designation ensures clear organizational accountability for ensuring full compliance with mandatory registration, workplace welfare provisions, and wage disbursements.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the fundamental objectives of the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970:
I. To abolish contract labour wherever possible and practicable.
II. To ensure that contractors operate without the need for government licensing.
III. To regulate the working conditions of contract labour where abolition is not possible.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
options_english: I and II only
I and III only
II and III only
I, II and III all
questions.explanation_english: The fundamental objectives of the Act are to regulate the employment of contract labour in establishments where complete abolition is not feasible and to abolish contract labour in processes where abolition is practicable. Contractors are strictly required to obtain official licenses rather than operating without oversight, ensuring full regulatory compliance and statutory worker protection.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (c) है। अधिनियम के मौलिक उद्देश्यों में उन प्रतिष्ठानों में संविदा श्रम के रोजगार को विनियमित करना शामिल है जहाँ पूर्ण उन्मूलन संभव नहीं है और उन प्रक्रियाओं में संविदा श्रम का उन्मूलन करना शामिल है जहाँ उन्मूलन व्यावहारिक है। ठेकेदारों को बिना निगरानी के काम करने की अनुमति नहीं है, जिससे पूर्ण नियामक अनुपालन और कानूनी श्रमिक सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित होती है।
questions.topic: Contract Labour Abolition and Regulation Act 1970
key_facts: Section 10 aims to regulate employment of contract labour.
Printed answer key: (C) I and III only

Payment in kind, such as providing free daily meals and shared worker accommodation
Any convertible foreign currency specified under the Foreign Exchange Management Act

The Industrial Tribunal / Labour Court under the Industrial Disputes Act

questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (d) है। धारा 10(2) के अनुसार, उचित सरकार को यह विचार करना आवश्यक है कि कार्य स्थायी, सहायक या प्रतिष्ठान के लिए आवश्यक है, जो सामान्यतः नियमित श्रमिकों द्वारा किया जाता है, और क्या यह पूर्णकालिक श्रमिकों की एक महत्वपूर्ण संख्या को रोजगार देने के लिए पर्याप्त है। यह सुनिश्चित करता है कि अनुबंध श्रम पर रोक लगाने का निर्णय कार्य की प्रकृति और कार्यबल की आवश्यकताओं के गहन मूल्यांकन पर आधारित हो।

questions.question_english: In case a dispute arises whether any work performed in an establishment is of an intermittent or casual nature, who has the authority to decide this question?
options_english: The Principal Employer
The Appropriate Government
The Labour Court
The High Court of the respective State
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 1(5) of the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970, if a question arises whether any work performed in an establishment is of an intermittent or casual nature, the decision lies with the Appropriate Government. The government decides this matter after consulting the relevant Advisory Board, and its statutory decision remains final and binding.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (b) है। अनुबंध श्रम (नियमन और उन्मूलन) अधिनियम, 1970 की धारा 1(5) के तहत, यदि किसी प्रतिष्ठान में किए गए कार्य के अंतराल या आकस्मिक स्वभाव के बारे में प्रश्न उठता है, तो निर्णय उचित सरकार के पास होता है। सरकार इस मामले का निर्णय संबंधित सलाहकार बोर्ड से परामर्श करने के बाद करती है, और इसका वैधानिक निर्णय अंतिम और बाध्यकारी होता है।
questions.topic: Contract Labour Abolition and Regulation Act 1970
key_facts: Section 1(5) addresses disputes regarding work nature.
Appropriate Government has the final authority.

Printed answer key: (B) The Appropriate Government

questions.explanation_english: The correct answer is (a). The Proviso to Section 1(4) empowers the appropriate Government to extend the application of the Act to any establishment or contractor employing less than twenty workmen. This extension requires giving not less than two months’ notice of intention by official gazette notification, providing flexibility to broaden worker protections where necessary to prevent exploitation in smaller operations.

questions.question_english: A Government School in Delhi engages an agency for gardening. The agency deploys 5 gardeners for 45 days during the monsoon season. Does the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970 apply to the school as a Principal Employer for this specific contract?
options_english: Yes, because it is a government establishment and the Act applies universally to all public sector bodies.
Yes, because the routine work of maintaining school grounds and gardening is deemed perennial in nature.
No, because all educational institutions and government schools are completely exempt from the Act.
No, because the number of workmen is less.
questions.explanation_english: The Central Act applies only to establishments employing twenty or more contract workmen. Moreover, Section 1(5) exempts intermittent work, and seasonal work under sixty days is deemed intermittent. Since the school engaged only five gardeners for forty-five days, it falls below the minimum numerical threshold and meets intermittent criteria, excluding it from statutory coverage.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (d) है। केंद्रीय अधिनियम केवल उन प्रतिष्ठानों पर लागू होता है जो बीस या अधिक संविदा श्रमिकों को रोजगार देते हैं। इसके अलावा, धारा 1(5) अंतराल कार्य को छूट देती है, और 60 दिनों से कम का मौसमी कार्य अंतराल कार्य माना जाता है। चूंकि स्कूल ने केवल 45 दिनों के लिए 5 माली नियुक्त किए, यह न्यूनतम संख्या के थ्रेशोल्ड से नीचे है और अंतराल मानदंडों को पूरा करता है, जिससे इसे वैधानिक कवरेज से बाहर रखा गया है।
questions.topic: Contract Labour Abolition and Regulation Act 1970
key_facts: The Act applies to establishments with 20 or more contract workers.
Intermittent work is exempt under Section 1(5).
Printed answer key: (D) No, because the number of workmen is less.
